name: Regem-Melek
title: Envoyed to Bethel
summary: Regem-Melek was one of the men sent by the people of Bethel to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem to seek the Lord's favor and to ask the priests and prophets whether they should continue to fast and mourn in the fifth month, as they had done during the exile. His inquiry led to an important prophetic message from Zechariah about true righteousness rather than ritual fasting.

keyEvents.title: Sent to the House of the Lord
keyEvents.description: Regem-Melek was sent together with Sharezer and their men by the people of Bethel to implore the Lord for favor.

keyEvents.title: Question about Fasting
keyEvents.description: Regem-Melek and his delegation asked the priests and prophets whether they should still observe the fast in the fifth month as they had done for many years during the exile.

keyEvents.title: The Lord's Answer through Zechariah
keyEvents.description: In response to their question, the Lord spoke through the prophet Zechariah and questioned the motivation behind the fast—whether it was truly directed toward the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Call to Righteousness over Rituals
keyEvents.description: The Lord used the opportunity to exhort the people to true righteousness: to judge fairly, show mercy and compassion, and not oppress the weak.

keyEvents.title: Warning about the Ancestors' Disobedience
keyEvents.description: God reminded through Zechariah that the ancestors had refused to listen to the earlier prophets, which led to God's anger and exile.
